title: Experience
description: A realistic engineering situation the learner is responsible for - not a chapter to read. Every experience has a starting state, a mission, expected investigation and decisions, and explicit success/failure conditions. outcome_refs may be empty for a blueprint-only catalog entry; it is populated only once an experience is fully specified with learning outcomes and artifacts.

future_capability_domains.description: Free-text domain slugs this experience will eventually also reference once those stub domains are authored. Not id-validated - intentionally honest about current gaps rather than inventing unresolvable references.

learner_problem.description: Optional. The single-sentence problem framing this experience teaches the learner to answer (e.g. 'why pod autoscaling is not enough for GPU workloads'). Distinct from scenario/learner_mission, which describe a specific situation - this states the transferable question.

core_concept.description: Optional. The one core conceptual distinction this experience is built around, stated plainly enough to be the experience's single takeaway if a learner remembered nothing else.

mental_model.description: Optional. An ordered causal chain (each entry one step) the learner should be able to reproduce afterward - e.g. 'traffic increases' -> 'KEDA increases pod replicas' -> 'scheduler checks node capacity' -> 'insufficient capacity -> pods Pending' -> 'Karpenter provisions a node' -> 'pods schedule'.

system_architecture.description: Optional. An ordered list of the components the learner must be able to name and place before the scenario makes sense (e.g. Users, ALB, Service, Pods, Model Server, GPU, KEDA, Scheduler, Karpenter).

prerequisite_knowledge.description: Optional. What the learner must already know (distinct from target_learner_profiles/prerequisites, which are learner-band and experience-graph references) for this experience's teaching content to land.

learning_sequence.description: Optional. The named stages this experience's teaching content walks through in order (e.g. architecture -> healthy operation -> failure -> node-level scaling -> expert reasoning -> recap), each with what that stage is responsible for teaching.

key_takeaways.description: Optional. The short list of statements a learner should be able to make unprompted after finishing this experience.

misconceptions.description: Optional. Specific wrong mental models learners commonly bring to this topic, paired with the correction - distinct from expected_decisions' plausible-but-wrong options, which are scenario-specific rather than general misconceptions.

evidence_of_understanding.description: Optional. Observable signs a learner has actually internalized core_concept/mental_model - distinct from evidence_of_competence, which is scenario-specific proof of having completed the mission.
